solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Demanding, like the Queen's partner?

blocks.note: 'as' is a word meaning 'like', in the sense of being similar to
a king partners a queen, on a throne or on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A question about whether a demanding person behaves like royalty's consort.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split: the answer read as two words describes someone resembling a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asking a lot of you is being demanding; the participle of 'ask' works as a synonym here.

clue.text: With a wedge, you'll get many holes in one!

definitions.text: With a wedge, you'll get many holes in one!

blocks.clueFragment: With a wedge, you'll get many holes in one!
blocks.note: surface reading: a golfer using a wedge club and sinking aces

blocks.clueFragment: With a wedge, you'll get many holes in one!
blocks.note: setter's reading: a wedge-shaped slice of a famously holey dairy product, riddled with holes

explanation.surface: A golf boast that a wedge club will bring you plenty of holes in one.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedge and holes in one belong to golf, but here the wedge is a slice of Emmental-style cheese, full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental, the classic Swiss variety, is known for the large air pockets that riddle every slice.

clue.text: White House soldier going round facilities

indicators.note: turning round makes the soldier face the other way, so his short name is read backwards

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
'facilities' is a polite word for a toilet, a loo in British slang

explanation.surface: A soldier at the President's residence makes a tour of the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' looks like Washington, but is a snow house, white because it is built of snow blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome dwelling is built from blocks of snow, so it is literally a house that is white.

clue.text: Continue to talk French art with East African

blocks.note: to gab on is to keep chattering
'tu es' is French for 'thou art'
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Chattering on about French painting with someone from East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East African' reads as one phrase, but East only gives a letter; Gabon is in fact on Africa's west coast. 'Art' is the old verb form, as in 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Gabon, a central African nation, is a Gabonese, so the word is a demonym for an African.

clue.text: Attend Congress or get out of town

blocks.note: to attend an event is to be present there, two words split as 'be at'
congress can mean sexual intercourse, which is 'it' in slang

explanation.surface: An ultimatum: show up to the legislature or leave the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature but means sexual congress, and 'it' is crossword slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word imperative is slang telling someone to go away, just as 'get out of town' does.

clue.text: Song everyone gets in Michael Jackson album

indicators.note: one thing getting in to another ends up sitting inside it

blocks.note: Bad is Michael Jackson's 1987 album
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Every listener finds some track to love on a Michael Jackson record.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, often a slow sentimental one or one telling a story.

clue.text: A miserable cold

blocks.note: taken as written
pathetic means miserable, pitiful

explanation.surface: A complaint about a nasty, wretched head cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like the illness the miserable sufferer has; it is the definition, meaning indifferent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cold in manner shows no feeling or interest, which is what being indifferent and unmoved means.

clue.text: Fish that's full of bone-strengthening vitamin

indicators.note: a thing full of something has it inside, wrapping around it

blocks.note: i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'
vitamin D helps build strong bones

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a fish that is rich in vitamins good for the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family, also called an orfe.

clue.text: Article I type up under pressure, at great speed

indicators.note: things that are up in the air are thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A journalist typing up a story in a rush, working under deadline pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The pressure letter joins the other thirteen-minus-one letters in one shuffle; 'under' only links it to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting precipitately is acting hastily or headlong, with too much speed and too little thought.

clue.text: Bigoted Illinois artist involved in defamation

indicators.note: someone involved in an affair is caught up inside it

blocks.note: IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois
libel is written defamation
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A prejudiced painter from Illinois caught up in a libel case.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means intolerant and narrow-minded, which describes a bigoted outlook.

clue.text: I want attention in the morning, man admitted

indicators.note: someone admitted is let inside, here into a time of day

blocks.note: a.m. denotes the morning
a man is a he

explanation.surface: Someone at the door at breakfast time demanding notice once let in.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat-clearing sound is the conventional way to signal 'notice me' politely, an interjection request.

clue.text: Small court writ in article about to go out?

indicators.note: something written in is entered within a space, so it goes inside

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
S is the abbreviation for small
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A small court document set out in a newspaper piece about something going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' here means to lose consciousness; the question mark admits the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a faint is on the point of passing out, so 'about to go out' describes them.

clue.text: Tread softly after awful char's periodic digs

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters of chars
to pad is to walk with soft steps

explanation.surface: Walking quietly behind a dreadful cleaner, perhaps an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a cleaning woman in British usage; digs is British for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is a place to sleep now and then, an occasional lodging rather than a home.

clue.text: Yes I'm fat and I've far to travel

indicators.note: letters sent travelling move around and end up rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are overweight and have a long journey ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative is a reply meaning agreement, the formal or radio word for a positive response.

clue.text: OK, let's get ready to hitchhike!

blocks.note: first meaning: a gesture signalling approval
second meaning, read playfully: the raised digits a hitchhiker shows to drivers

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: a hitchhiker raises a hand with the digit pointing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The gesture of raised thumbs signals approval, and is also the pose a roadside hitcher holds out.

clue.text: It might help one to get off horse

definitions.text: It might help one to get off horse

blocks.clueFragment: It might help one to get off horse
blocks.note: surface reading: an aid for dismounting from a mount

blocks.clueFragment: It might help one to get off horse
blocks.note: setter's reading: horse is slang for heroin, and this is the substitute drug used to wean addicts off it

explanation.surface: Something like a mounting block that helps a rider climb down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is slang for heroin, and 'get off' means quit an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic opioid is prescribed as a substitute in treatment programmes for heroin addiction.

clue.text: Late president behind on time

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first-named piece is placed second

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A dead president who was running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'behind on time' puts the word for behind after the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th US president, long dead, hence 'late'.

clue.text: Sleeping after bit of strenuous exercise

indicators.note: a small bit of a word here means just its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of strenuous
kipping is British slang for sleeping

explanation.surface: Having a nap after a short burst of hard workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for a sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping a rope is a familiar form of exercise, used by boxers and children alike.

clue.text: Ham possibly putting Come Together over the air

indicators.note: something sent over the air is broadcast, so it is heard rather than read

blocks.note: to come together is to meet

explanation.surface: An amateur radio operator broadcasting the Beatles song Come Together.
explanation.walkthrough: A ham is also a radio amateur, which suits 'over the air'; here it is pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham is one example of meat, and 'possibly' marks it as an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Catch around about so long

blocks.note: to catch is to take
ca. is circa, around
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Fragments of instructions about catching something round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around about' looks like one idiom but gives two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual farewells said when parting, so one goodbye phrase stands for the other.

clue.text: Peak hot time of the day

blocks.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot
eight o'clock is a time of the day

explanation.surface: The warmest part of the day is its peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the highest point, and height can mean a summit or the utmost degree.

clue.text: Declining November temperature going beyond 40s?

blocks.note: the forties are a decade
N is November in the NATO alphabet
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Late-autumn temperatures exceeding forty degrees, and dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 40s looks like degrees but is the decade of the 1940s or one's forties.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes a society in moral decline, falling away from former standards.

clue.text: You must get out of big tree

indicators.note: something told to get out of a place has to leave it, so it is removed

blocks.note: U is text-speak for you
big in the sense of well-liked, successful

explanation.surface: A warning to leave a large tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big tree' looks like one description, but big is the word that loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree, of the willow family, common along European roads.

clue.text: Quiet chap with a salty wife "saint" beds

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical term for quiet
in Genesis, Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A quiet man whose wife is foul-mouthed and saintly in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Salty suggests crude language, but refers to the Bible story where Lot's wife looked back and became salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden plots are small areas of ground for planting, the same as beds of flowers or vegetables.

clue.text: British port and spirit

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A list of drinks: a British port wine and a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Port and spirit both look like drinks; port is a harbour city and spirit is the definition, meaning verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is liveliness and vigour, the kind of spirit a performer plays with.

clue.text: Rag and bone

blocks.note: first meaning: to tease someone
second meaning: one of the curved bones of the chest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag and bone' suggests the British rag-and-bone man, a junk collector; the words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease them, and a rib is also a bone of the ribcage.

clue.text: Nettle I chop back on island peninsula

indicators.note: going back means reading the word for chop in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to nettle is to annoy or gall
taken as written
to lop is to chop off
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Cutting back stinging weeds on an island with a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: Nettle looks like the plant but is the verb, to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a peninsula in Turkey, site of the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: A disposition to pinch soprano, but not there

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip something tightly, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a bent is a natural inclination or disposition
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to steal from a soprano who is not present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is missing or away, so the word means not present at a place.

clue.text: Truth drug Bojo has GP give Nigel (at last!)

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of each word that comes before

blocks.clueFragment: drug Bojo has GP give Nigel
blocks.note: the final letters of drug, Bojo, has, GP, give and Nigel

explanation.surface: A doctor finally prescribes truth serum to Boris Johnson for Nigel Farage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bojo is Boris Johnson's nickname and Nigel suggests Farage; the brackets make 'at last' look like an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel means something absolutely true, as in taking a statement as gospel truth.
